transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Start: 15:30 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: James Park (Redwood AE), Maya Srinivasan (Redwood SE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood Product), Priya Desai (Avalon Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Avalon Platform), Evelyn Zhou (Avalon SecOps)
Recording ID: ff-20261211-avalon-01

Summary (auto): quick Optimize walkthrough focused on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, quality vs latency tradeoffs, and pilot next steps. Customer wants to validate latency SLOs on their 1k qps-ish workload and confirm security posture for VPC/Dedicated deployment.

Transcript:
[00:00] James: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intro, I'm James Park on the AE side, with Maya our solutions engineer, Carlos from product. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good thanks. Excited to see the quantization discussion — we've been hearing a lot about INT8 and FP8 tradeoffs.
[00:12] Maya: Great. Today we'll walk through redwood's Optimize recommendations for quant profiles, show some benchmark numbers, and discuss how quality degrades — or doesn't — across INT8/FP8. We'll also talk deployment options, dedicated vs hosted, VPC, KMS, audit logs.
[00:24] Liam: Quick ask, our main SLO is 250ms p95 for the chat completions on a 1k daily qps pattern, sometimes spikes. Cost is also a constraint.
[00:33] Carlos: Noted. That informs batching/kv cache decisions too.
[00:36] Maya: Right. Ok, slide deck up — link in chat: https://redwood.ai/optimize/avalon-quant-bench (note: link is internal demo slide).

[00:45] Maya: First principles — FP8 keeps more dynamic range than INT8 so quality often holds up better for difficult instructions but at higher memory/compute. INT8 gives best cost and throughput but you can see quality regressions for certain heads, long-context summarization, and numeric precision.
[01:05] Priya: For our summarization flows, we care about hallucination rates and factuality, not just BLEU. Any guidance?
[01:12] Maya: Yep. We recommend running prompt/eval suites against candidate quant profiles. In our internal tests, with a 7B class model, INT8 increased short-form hallucination by ~3-5% on our evals, whereas FP8 was within 1% of float32. But on classification tasks the gap was negligible.
[01:33] James: To translate that — if your workload is retrieval+generation with long context, FP8 may be safer; for short chat and high throughput INT8 often wins.
[01:44] Liam: How much latency delta are we talking?
[01:46] Maya: On a 1x A100 style baseline, INT8 reduced token latency by about 20-30% vs FP8 in our benchmark (with identical batching). On Ampere GPUs and with optimized kernels you might see slightly different numbers; hardware + sequence length matter.
[02:05] Priya: Our sequence lengths average 512 tokens, tail to 2k. Will that blow up INT8 problems?
[02:10] Maya: Yeah longer KV cache increases memory pressure; INT8 helps with memory but quantization error can compound on long contexts. For 2k tails we often recommend a hybrid: FP8 for steps where quality sensitive, INT8 for cached prefixes. Redwood Optimize supports mixed profiles per route.
[02:27] Evelyn: Security question — if we go dedicated in our VPC, do we still see audit logs and token-level cost breakdowns? Also KMS for key management?
[02:35] Carlos: Yes for Dedicated we support customer-managed VPC, KMS/HSM integrations, and we push audit logs to your S3 or SIEM. We'll share the SOC2 + VPC deployment guide after the call.
[02:47] Evelyn: Ok that helps. Any regulatory caveats around FP8 since it's still relatively new?
[02:52] James: Nothing specific — quant format isn't regulatory, what matters is reproducibility and audit trails. We'll include details on model checkpoints and exact quant seeds used in the pilot report.

[03:05] Maya: Now I'll go through a quick benchmark table — apologies transcription may be off, numbers are approximate here but raw CSV will be shared. Example: Model X (7B): float32 p95=340ms, FP8 p95=360ms, INT8 p95=270ms; quality delta (avg score) FP8 -0.8%, INT8 -3.7% on our eval set.
[03:28] Priya: Are those with batching? What batch size?
[03:30] Maya: Those were batch=1 single-stream p95 numbers. Batch=4 gives more throughput and INT8 benefits grow. We can test with your real distribution.
[03:40] Liam: For us p95 on single-stream matters because we do interactive web UI. Batching is possible at backend for async jobs.
[03:48] Maya: Understood — we can tune per-route: keep low-latency routes on FP8 or float, and heavy async ingestion on INT8.

[04:00] James: Let's address cost — rough estimates: INT8 reduces VM/GPU memory footprint, often letting you fit more concurrency per instance which reduces per-token cost by ~25-40% depending on model and infra. FP8 is in the middle.
[04:14] Priya: Do you support automated profiling — like Redwood Optimize recommending a profile per route?
[04:18] Carlos: Yes, Optimize includes a profiler that ingests traces and suggests quant profiles, batching, and caching config. It produces a report with quality vs latency curves and recommended tradeoffs.
[04:30] Priya: Great — can we see the profiler output on our corpus?
[04:33] Maya: We'll run a profiler as part of the pilot. Maya notes: need sample queries and expected SLOs.

[04:40] [05:00] (background) Speaker overlap, unclear words, slight cross talk
[05:05] Priya: One more technical — does Redwood do per-layer quant calibration or simple post-training static quant?
[05:11] Maya: We support both. For INT8 we usually do per-layer calibration with a small calibration set; for FP8 it tends to be dynamic range scaling at runtime. Per-layer calibration reduces quality regressions.
[05:24] Priya: Good. Do you persist calibration artifacts so runs are reproducible?
[05:28] Carlos: Yes, calibration tables and exact kernel versions are stored as part of the model bundle in the deployment manifest. That goes into the audit artifact.

[05:40] Liam: If we want to start with hosted API for quick testing, then move to Dedicated VPC, is that a supported path? How long would migration take?
[05:51] James: That's a common pattern. Hosted + Optimize for profiling/pilot, then Dedicated reserved pools for production. Migration depends on model size and infra but typically a few days to a couple weeks for full validation; we'll work with your infra team.
[06:05] Evelyn: For Dedicated, do you offer HSM-backed KMS?
[06:09] Carlos: Yes, we integrate with customer HSM/KMS via standard APIs and support rotate/bring-your-own-key.

[06:18] Maya: Ok, quick demo clipboard — showing raw benchmark CSV (link in chat) and an example Optimize report. Example screenshot shows quality vs latency curve where INT8 curve is shifted left (lower latency) but dips in quality for tail cases. FP8 sits closer to float32.
[06:40] Priya: Can the Optimize report highlight hallucination regressions specifically?
[06:43] Maya: Yes if you feed in an eval set labeled for hallucination or factuality, Optimize will report per-metric deltas. If you don't have labels we can run fuzzy heuristics but labeled eval is better.
[06:54] Priya: We have a small labeled set for hallucination; we'll share.

[07:00] James: Next steps and timeline — propose pilot: (1) Avalon sends 2k sample queries + SLOs by 12/14, (2) Redwood runs profiler and 3 quant configs (float/FP8/INT8) and returns a report by 12/18, (3) review results and decide route-based profile and pilot for two routes.
[07:19] Priya: That timeline looks fine.
[07:21] James: I'll also send pricing for Dedicated and estimated cost delta per-token for INT8 vs FP8.
[07:27] Evelyn: Please include security docs and where audit logs land.
[07:30] James: Will do.

[07:35] (wrap) Carlos: Any final Qs?
[07:37] Liam: No, thanks.
[07:39] Priya: Thanks everyone, looking forward.
[07:41] James: Great — we'll follow up with the CSV and SOC2 + VPC doc and schedule the pilot run.

[07:50] End recording.

Notes about transcript quality: Automated transcription missed some technical terms (e.g., exact model architecture names) and there is occasional mis-attribution. Raw benchmark CSV and Optimize PDF will be attached separately.
